entries.name: Mail-merge batch automation
entries.scenario: A marketing workstation runs a Word mail-merge that shells out to cmd.exe to post-process recipient CSV files exported from the CRM.
entries.evidence: ParentImage is WINWORD.EXE and the child is cmd.exe, but the command line references the mail-merge tool path; events cluster during campaign windows and originate from marketing workstations only.
entries.tuning: Exclude the mail-merge tool's command-line pattern, scoped to the marketing OU. Revisit quarterly - if the tool is replaced, the exclusion should die with it.

entries.name: Legacy Excel reporting add-in
entries.scenario: An old line-of-business Excel add-in launches wscript.exe to render reports whenever finance opens specific workbooks.
entries.evidence: ParentImage is EXCEL.EXE and the child is wscript.exe with the same script path across events; a single finance user group is affected and the workbook filenames are report-related.
entries.tuning: Exclude the add-in's script path, and file a ticket to migrate the reporting - this is technical debt that should eventually be retired rather than permanently tuned out.

entries.name: Deployment script using Invoke-Expression
entries.scenario: A provisioning script legitimately downloads a configuration module and runs it via Invoke-Expression - matching the rule's DownloadString-plus-IEX pattern.
entries.evidence: CommandLine contains both DownloadString and IEX, but the URL points at the internal package mirror and the executing account is the deployment tool's service account.
entries.tuning: Exclude the internal mirror hostname for that service account only - never exclude the account itself. Give the exclusion an expiry date and prefer rewriting the script to avoid IEX.
